card.name: "No" opening dose-adjustment statements
card.fires_on: The word "No" (or "no") starting a sentence right after a hepatic or renal impairment heading or sentence, just before "dose adjustment" or "dosage adjustment".

modes.label: No adjustment after impairment heading
modes.description: "No" begins the statement that no dose change is needed, directly after an organ-impairment heading or a reduced-dose sentence.
modes.example: 2.6 Dosage Adjustment in Patients with Hepatic Impairment<< No>> dose adjustment of UPTRAVI is

modes.label: No adjustment after a colon or comma
modes.description: "no" follows a colon or comma that follows a severity grade, such as mild impairment or Child-Pugh class.
modes.example: Mild renal impairment (creatinine clearance of 60 to 89 mL/min):<< no>> dosage adjustment recommended

card.writes: It pushes toward unusual word pieces and away from words like repeated or warnings, so it gives no clear help for the next word.
card.plain: It marks the word "No" that begins a statement that no dose change is needed for kidney or liver impairment.
